documents.unit: Office of the Provost, Faculty Affairs / CTLE
documents.title: Gen AI and Teaching Guidelines - Faculty
documents.summary: Provost-office guidance (updated October 2024) telling faculty to put a Gen AI statement in every syllabus and leaving the stance to instructors, even per assignment. Also gives instructor-side advice on responsibility, data privacy under FERPA, accessibility and AI limitations. Unauthorized or undocumented AI use is treated as honor-system misconduct.
documents.stance_why: The guidance sets no stance of its own: 'The goal of these guidelines is not to set hard do's and don'ts', and 'It is the instructor's prerogative whether they choose to prohibit its use, allow its use with transparency/acknowledgment by students, or actively include its use'. It offers a non-official sample statement but no tiers, so delegates.

units.why: The guidelines call themselves non-binding: 'not to set hard do's and don'ts, but to provide guidance and have conversations'. This states the document's purpose and scope, so a framework type with informs modality and neutral stance.
units.anchor: The goal of these guidelines is not to set hard

units.why: 'these guidelines may be updated and/or revised accordingly' says the guidance is provisional, which is the revisit-regularly type.
units.anchor: these guidelines may be updated and/or revised accordingly

units.why: A faculty advisory committee 'was formed to deliberate on the fast pace of changes in the AI arena', which describes the body behind the guidance, so P84 (how and by whom the policy was made).
units.anchor: was formed to deliberate on the fast pace of changes in the AI arena

units.why: The committee provides 'hands-on workshops and sessions' for faculty, which is support for faculty learning AI (P63), not a rule for students.
units.anchor: providing continued guidance, including hands-on workshops and sessions

units.why: 'it benefits faculty and students to develop AI literacy' argues AI skills matter for the organizations students join, so the career-skill rationale type P44.
units.anchor: it benefits faculty and students to develop AI literacy

units.why: Faculty are 'encouraged' to keep fostering students' learning of essential materials and critical thinking while using AI; the intent is that AI not displace student thinking, nearest to P32.
units.anchor: we also encourage faculty to continue actively fostering students’ ongoing learning of essential materials
units.fit_note: Addressed to faculty as a duty to keep fostering learning, not to students as primary problem-solvers.

units.why: 'it is imperative to help our students develop AI literacy ... required for future careers' is the professional-skill rationale (P44) and an instructor duty.
units.anchor: it is imperative to help our students develop AI literacy

units.why: Students are to be reminded that 'unauthorized use of these tools constitutes academic misconduct', which classifies misuse as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: unauthorized use of these tools constitutes academic misconduct

units.why: The guidelines 'recognize the need to specifically include a Gen AI statement in your course syllabi', an expectation that every syllabus carry an AI statement (P09).
units.anchor: specifically include a Gen AI statement in your course syllabi

units.why: Where AI is part of the curriculum, 'both instructors and students understand how to use these resources effectively, appropriately, and ethically'; this expects effective AI use as a skill, so P44.
units.anchor: it is expected that both instructors and students understand how to use these resources effectively

units.why: A 'university syllabus statement that should be included in all syllabi' is a required-in-every-syllabus rule (P09); the document does not say what that statement contains.
units.anchor: university syllabus statement that should be included in all syllabi

units.why: 'we offer the following statement that you might choose to include' supplies sample syllabus language (P110); the text adds that it is 'not an official VCU policy', so it is non-binding.
units.anchor: not an official VCU policy; instead it is guidance

units.why: The suggested statement says instructors 'may choose to provide specific guidelines ... or not permit', so the decision is left per instructor (P04).
units.anchor: Instructors may choose to provide specific guidelines for use of GEN AI tools

units.why: 'Instructors must be clear about their expectations' requires stated expectations per assignment or overall (P09).
units.anchor: Instructors must be clear about their expectations

units.why: A student who finds a tool's appropriateness 'ambiguous or unclear' 'must seek clarification from the instructor before using it', the ask-first type P10.
units.anchor: they must seek clarification from the instructor before using it for an assignment

units.why: Unauthorized, undocumented or uncited Gen AI use is 'considered academic misconduct', including cheating and plagiarism; P36 fits better than P28 because it classifies misuse rather than addressing penalty for disclosure.
units.anchor: are considered academic misconduct
units.fit_note: Also implies that missing documentation or citation is itself misconduct (P28 aspect).

units.why: 'violates the VCU Honor System' ties breach of an instructor's course AI policy to the existing honor system, i.e. misconduct handling (P36).
units.anchor: violates an instructor’s course policies and/or guidelines violates the VCU Honor System

units.why: 'each faculty member should directly address policies about the use of Gen AI in their course syllabus' is the AI-statement-in-every-syllabus rule (P09), stated again as applying 'whether or not' they use AI.
units.anchor: each faculty member should directly address policies about the use of Gen AI

units.why: 'It is the instructor's prerogative whether they choose to prohibit its use, allow its use with transparency/acknowledgment by students, or actively include its use', which sets the decision per instructor (P04).
units.anchor: It is the instructor’s prerogative whether they choose to prohibit its use

units.why: Faculty 'may vary the use of, or deny the use of, Gen AI tools across course assignments/assessments', so the rule can differ per assignment; P04 includes per-assignment choice.
units.anchor: faculty may vary the use of, or deny the use of, Gen AI tools

units.why: 'should be clearly communicated for each deliverable' asks for assignment-level communication of the AI rule (P09).
units.anchor: should be clearly communicated for each deliverable

units.why: 'different courses will have different policies' is the statement that one course's rules do not carry to others (P11); instructors are told to remind students.
units.anchor: different courses will have different policies

units.why: Faculty are advised to 'refer students to the Gen AI Guidelines for Students' and the syllabus at the semester start, pointing to further guidance (P115).
units.anchor: faculty review, and refer students to,

units.why: 'Gen AI should not be used as a substitute for your own teaching' limits instructor AI use in teaching work (P59).
units.anchor: Gen AI should not be used as a substitute for your own teaching

units.why: 'you are 100% responsible for the teaching materials' even if built with Gen AI sets instructor accountability for AI-made materials, nearest P48 (review of AI-made materials).
units.anchor: you are 100% responsible for the teaching materials
units.fit_note: States instructor responsibility for materials, not an explicit review or disclosure duty.

units.why: 'faculty should consider citing/acknowledging their own use of AI' asks instructors to disclose their own AI use (P47).
units.anchor: faculty should consider citing/acknowledging their own use of AI

units.why: Faculty should 'Encourage the use of Gen AI in ways that will inspire critical thinking and creativity ... not pose as a substitute for genuine learning'; the point is that AI must not replace learning, nearest P41.
units.anchor: not pose as a substitute for genuine learning
units.fit_note: Frames a positive use (AI that inspires critical thinking) alongside the warning, not only a limit.

units.why: 'Expectations for ethical and responsible use should always be emphasized, as well as modeled by the instructor' makes instructors model responsible use (P112).
units.anchor: as well as modeled by the instructor

units.why: 'If you have used Gen AI when creating certain course materials, acknowledge its use' asks instructors to tell students about AI-made materials (P47).
units.anchor: acknowledge its use

units.why: Faculty are told to 'critically assess the overall quality' of AI-assisted assignments and grading material; this is instructor guidance on using AI in teaching work (P59).
units.anchor: faculty should critically assess the overall quality of what has been created

units.why: 'entering personal data or other confidential information is a security risk' is a privacy warning that instructors pass to students (P50).
units.anchor: entering personal data or other confidential information is a security risk

units.why: 'AI systems cannot guarantee data privacy' and have no standard security protocols, a factual privacy statement (P50).
units.anchor: AI systems cannot guarantee data privacy

units.why: 'all work submitted by students is protected under FERPA, and therefore cannot be uploaded to a Gen AI tool without their written consent' binds instructors; P50 (protect data) is nearest.
units.anchor: cannot be uploaded to a Gen AI tool without their written consent
units.fit_note: Targets instructors uploading student work, and cites FERPA.

units.why: The FERPA rule is extended to 'Gen AI detection tools, unless VCU has a contract with the provider', which limits detectors by contract (P65, review of tools).
units.anchor: unless VCU has a contract with the provider
units.fit_note: Limits use of detection tools to those under a university contract rather than reviewing tools generally.

units.why: Students 'can upload their own graded materials' into tools but it 'is not recommended' without a contract, a student-level data caution (P50).
units.anchor: Students, however, can upload their own graded materials into such tools.
units.fit_note: Permits the upload but advises against it absent a contract.

units.why: 'Always ensure that your Gen AI resources/materials support your course objectives/outcomes' links AI decisions to learning objectives (P83).
units.anchor: support your course objectives/outcomes

units.why: 'Regularly assess the impact of using AI in your course and student learning outcomes' and adjust, which is collecting evidence on AI's effect on learning (P55).
units.anchor: Regularly assess the impact of using AI in your course

units.why: Faculty must 'Confirm that Gen AI resources that you suggest or require ... are not biased, prejudiced, or inaccurate', evaluating tools before choosing them (P117).
units.anchor: Confirm that Gen AI resources that you suggest or require

units.why: 'accessible and freely available for all students, to ensure equitable access' concerns access and cost, P51.
units.anchor: accessible and freely available for all students, to ensure equitable access

units.why: 'Ensure that AI usage does not disadvantage any students' and promotes inclusivity speaks to accessibility for diverse needs (P97); P51 is cost and equal access and does not name learning needs.
units.anchor: AI usage does not disadvantage any students

units.why: 'Keep yourself informed regarding development of new AI resources' is a duty to stay informed (P102).
units.anchor: Keep yourself informed regarding development of new AI resources

units.why: 'advises faculty to reflect on the ethical considerations' is a general call for ethical use with no specific content (P116).
units.anchor: advises faculty to reflect on the ethical considerations of using Gen AI

units.why: Ethical use includes 'using data in a responsible manner that complies with relevant regulations', a compliance rule (P77).
units.anchor: using data in a responsible manner that complies with relevant regulations

units.why: 'ownership of content generated by Gen AI remains unresolved at the federal level' is a statement about IP and ownership of output (P52).
units.anchor: ownership of content generated by Gen AI remains unresolved at the federal level

units.why: Gen AI is 'confidently wrong in its predictions' and weak at citations and math: output cannot be trusted without checks (P31).
units.anchor: Gen AI does not perform well with multiple elements
units.fit_note: Describes the limitation but does not tell users to verify.

units.why: 'the internal processes it uses to generate content are still unclear' names opacity as a limitation; nearest P31 (output reliability).
units.anchor: the internal processes it uses to generate content are still unclear
units.fit_note: About transparency of the model's process, not output errors.

units.why: Output 'may result in output that reflects biases, inaccuracies, or complete fabrication', a bias and harms statement (P53).
units.anchor: output that reflects biases, inaccuracies, or complete fabrication

units.why: 'the accuracy of tools that purportedly detect GenAI use is not guaranteed' states detectors are unreliable (P39).
units.anchor: the accuracy of tools that purportedly detect GenAI use is not guaranteed

units.why: Detectors 'may also exhibit inherent biases that can negatively impact certain groups of students (e.g., non-native English writers)', a fairness harm (P53).
units.anchor: inherent biases that can negatively impact certain groups of students

units.why: 'Faculty should exercise due diligence in understanding and addressing the multiple ethical considerations' is a general ethical-use call (P116).
units.anchor: Faculty should exercise due diligence in understanding and addressing

units.why: The CTLE promises to collate resources for faculty, a faculty-support commitment (P63).
units.anchor: We will be collating and making these available as resources

units.why: '(Guidelines regarding the use and procurement of Gen AI tools are also provided by the Office of the CIO)' directs readers to further guidance (P115).
units.anchor: procurement of Gen AI tools are also provided by the Office of the CIO

units.why: The acknowledgment names who drafted and edited the guidelines, which records how the guidance was made (P84).
units.anchor: Initial drafts and extensive edits of the guidelines were created by

documents.title: Generative AI at VCU
documents.summary: Technology Services page on generative AI at VCU: approved enterprise tools, data classification rules, FERPA limits on uploading student work, and vetting by IT Governance. On teaching it only points to instructor-given guidance and the provost guidelines.
documents.stance_why: The CIO page is mainly about data, tools and security, and says on teaching only that 'instructors will provide guidance for students on the appropriate use of AI for their course assignments', so the stance on student use is handed to instructors: delegates.

units.why: The CIO defines GenAI as 'systems that can create new content', which sets what the guidance covers (P61).
units.anchor: refers to systems that can create new content

units.why: 'VCU provides Google Gemini, Microsoft CoPilot, and Adobe Firefly through our enterprise licenses' names university-licensed tools (P92).
units.anchor: VCU provides Google Gemini, Microsoft CoPilot, and Adobe Firefly

units.why: 'Do not enter confidential (Category 1) or sensitive (Category 2) data into any AI tools unless they have been approved' is a data-protection prohibition (P50).
units.anchor: Do not enter confidential (Category 1) or sensitive (Category 2) data

units.why: 'Information given to generative AI tools is not private' warns that prompts are stored or reviewed (P50).
units.anchor: Information given to generative AI tools is not private

units.why: 'Adhere to current university guidelines and policies when using AI tools' requires following existing university policy (P77).
units.anchor: Adhere to current university guidelines and policies when using AI tools

units.why: The 'Acceptable Use of Generative AI Technology' policy 'establishes requirements and guardrails', an institution-wide framework (P56); the policy text itself is not in this document.
units.anchor: establishes requirements and guardrails for safe adoption and usage

units.why: 'Syllabus Statements dictate that instructors will provide guidance for students on the appropriate use of AI' is a university requirement that each course give AI guidance (P09).
units.anchor: instructors will provide guidance for students on the appropriate use of AI

units.why: 'It is prohibited to upload or use content that is copyrighted or infringes on the rights of any third party' is an IP prohibition (P52).
units.anchor: It is prohibited to upload or use content that is copyrighted

units.why: 'the university will continue to update its guidance and policies' commits to revisiting the policy (P54).
units.anchor: the university will continue to update its guidance and policies

units.why: 'Do not upload student work to Generative AI tools without written consent' protects student data under FERPA (P50).
units.anchor: Do not upload student work to Generative AI tools without written consent

units.why: Chats about VCU business 'can be subject to the Freedom of Information Act', including on personal accounts: a legal-compliance fact (P77).
units.anchor: they can be subject to the Freedom of Information Act

units.why: 'You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish' holds users accountable for what they submit, P29.
units.anchor: You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish

units.why: 'AI-generated content can be wrong or misleading' with fabrications and bias: the output-is-often-wrong warning (P31).
units.anchor: AI-generated content can be wrong or misleading

units.why: 'Check the generated content against reliable sources' tells users to verify output (P31).
units.anchor: Check the generated content against reliable sources

units.why: 'Do not trust AI data to give medical, legal, financial advice' warns against relying on AI for professional advice (P31).
units.anchor: Do not trust AI data to give medical, legal, financial advice
units.fit_note: Names domains where AI output must not be relied on.

units.why: 'Avoid using unauthorized third-party bots with Zoom and Google Meet' because meetings may be confidential; it is a use-vetted-tools rule (P92), not a consent rule.
units.anchor: Avoid using unauthorized third-party bots with Zoom and Google Meet
units.fit_note: Concerns AI meeting bots and transcription (P86 aspect) but about vetting, not consent.

units.why: 'VCU has vetted and approved the use of two transcription tools' names approved AI features for meetings (P92).
units.anchor: VCU has vetted and approved the use of two transcription tools

units.why: 'Learn the terms of service and privacy policies' of public AI systems is advice to evaluate a tool before use (P117).
units.anchor: Learn the terms of service and privacy policies
units.fit_note: Focuses on terms and data handling rather than accuracy or task fit.

units.why: The 'AI-enabled phishing' item says GenAI 'has made it easier for bad actors to create scams', security awareness (P75).
units.anchor: Generative AI has made it easier for bad actors to create scams

units.why: 'Send suspicious messages to infosec@vcu.edu' gives a reporting channel for AI-enabled threats (P71).
units.anchor: Send suspicious messages to infosec@vcu.edu

units.why: 'Any technology that stores, processes, or sends VCU data must have the required privacy, security and accessibility protections and be reviewed' sets institutional review before use (P65).
units.anchor: must have the required privacy, security and accessibility protections and be reviewed

units.why: 'Only use third-party tools that have been vetted and approved by IT Governance' restricts to approved tools (P92).
units.anchor: Only use third-party tools that have been vetted and approved by IT Governance

notes: Only the two included documents were coded. The Acceptable Use of Generative AI Technology policy text was not available. Course layer deferred in collect file.
